title: Your next medical scan could be from… Midjourney? 🩻👀 #trendingshorts #science #ai #tech #medical
description:
Midjourney, the company best known for its AI image models, announced a new division called Midjourney Medical and its first product is a full-body ultrasonic scanner. 

Patients descend into a shallow pool, passing through a ring of roughly half a million sensors that fire sound waves and capture echoes, reconstructing a 3D body map without radiation or magnets. 

The company claims near-MRI resolution at up to 100 times the speed and a few dollars per scan.

Developed with Butterfly Network, the scanner debuts at a "Midjourney Spa" in San Francisco in late 2027.

The scanner, developed with ultrasound chipmaker Butterfly Network, won't launch in a hospital but inside a wellness center called the "Midjourney Spa," opening in San Francisco in late 2027 alongside hot tubs, saunas, and cold plunges. 

Midjourney's long-term ambition is a fleet of 50,000 scanners performing a billion full-body scans a month, reframing medical imaging as something casual and routine rather than rare and expensive. 

If the technology delivers on its claims, it could shift medicine toward catching disease early in healthy people, though the scanner remains an unproven prototype that still needs clinical validation and FDA clearance for any diagnostic use.

top_reply.author: @charlesh5647
top_reply.text: The problem is just that there isn’t much actual imaging innovation here from midjourney. It’s essentially just a beefed up ultrasound with an ai model doing some math in the background to construct the final 3d rendering. The problem with this is that physics is fundamentally not on their side. Ultrasonic waves are not a good way to detect fine detail or variances in tissue structures. It’s just a semi accurate 3d map of hard internal structures. This in no way competes with or replaces the current medical scanning technology like MRI which uses various types of radiation to construct an incredibly accurate internal map of all its different tissues inside your body. So, they’ve basically invented a worse scanner that has few to none medical purposes which is why they have designated for exclusive use in health spas for body composition work. Basically helping you decide how best to exercise or do targeted fat loss treatments to sculpt around your bones which are harder to change. Is it kinda cool. Yes. Is the hype waranted. Absolutely not….
